title: You don’t fall into pride overnight.
paragraphs:
You don’t fall into pride overnight.
You drift into it… quietly.

And the most dangerous part?
You can still look “spiritual” while it’s happening.

You can still pray.
Still post verses.
Still show up at church.
But something inside you is shifting.
You don’t notice it at first.

It doesn’t feel like rebellion.
It feels like being right.

It feels like maturity.
Like discernment.
Like standing your ground.

But beneath that confidence…
there’s something growing.

As conviction.
As strength.
As “I just don’t tolerate nonsense anymore.”

There are moments now where correction irritates you more than it humbles you.
Where you silently compare yourself to others.
Where repentance feels slower than it used to.
And you don’t talk about it.
Some of you don’t feel far from God.
And that’s exactly where the danger is.

Because pride doesn’t say,
“I don’t need God.”

It says,
“I’m doing pretty well with God.”
You start measuring yourself against people instead of Scripture.

“At least I’m not like them.”
“I would never fall like that.”
“I’m more disciplined.”
“I actually take God seriously.”

Your standard shifts from God’s holiness
to other people’s failures.
That’s where pride begins to root itself.
Jesus exposed this in a story most people read too quickly.
“Two men went up to the temple to pray, one a Pharisee and the other a tax collector.” — Luke 18:10

One looked righteous.
The other looked broken.

One prayed with confidence.
The other couldn’t even lift his eyes.
“God, I thank You that I am not like other men…” — Luke 18:11
Because his prayer wasn’t centered on God.
“God, be merciful to me, a sinner!” — Luke 18:13

No comparison.
No performance.
No image.
And Jesus said something that should shake us:
“This man went down to his house justified, rather than the other.” — Luke 18:14
Because God resists pride—even when it wears religious clothing.
“God opposes the proud but gives grace to the humble.” — James 4:6

That means you can be active in church…
consistent in habits…
strong in knowledge…
…and still be in a position where God is resisting you.
But because pride is blocking what He wants to do in you.
And here’s how you know it’s happening.
When someone confronts you, you don’t pause.
You replay the conversation later—not to reflect, but to prove you were right.
“Whoever loves discipline loves knowledge, but whoever hates correction is stupid.” — Proverbs 12:1
Because correction is one of God’s primary tools to keep you aligned with truth.
You measure your walk based on how others are failing.
You feel secure when others fall.
You feel elevated when others struggle.
You just stop calling it sin.

“I’m just tired.”
“That’s just how I am.”
“They pushed me.”
“It’s not that serious.”
But the longer you delay repentance…
“Whoever conceals their sins does not prosper, but the one who confesses and renounces them finds mercy.” — Proverbs 28:13
And here’s the truth most people avoid:
You don’t lose your sensitivity to God overnight.
You lose it through unrepented moments.

Small compromises.
Small justifications.
Small delays in surrender.
But because pride started answering for you.
But this is where everything shifts.
Because the Gospel doesn’t just expose pride.
Your biggest problem isn’t your habits.
And no amount of discipline can save a proud heart.
“For all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God.” — Romans 3:23
“But God shows His love for us in that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.” — Romans 5:8
While you were still full of pride.
Jesus didn’t come for perfect people.
He came for proud people who are willing to become humble.
“If we confess our sins, He is faithful and just to forgive us our sins and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.” — 1 John 1:9
You are not stuck in pride.
You are one surrender away from grace.
Will you keep protecting your image?
Or will you let God transform your heart?
Will you keep comparing yourself to others?
Or will you stand honestly before a holy God?
God is not asking you to perform.
He’s asking you to come low.

Access to grace.
Access to healing.
Access to real transformation.
Right where you are, say it:
“Lord, expose every hidden pride in me.”
He will not reject that prayer.
He will meet you in it.
And what He builds after that…
From hidden pride to true surrender — because Jesus transforms what pride tried to protect.
